finds.quote: So the answer to I.31's open clause is available and nowhere stated: what division admits of syllogizing is the divine. Not by cutting God into pieces — the parts are χωριστὰ λόγῳ, separable in account, which is the mode De anima I.1 established for a soul whose divided parts go on living. God is not broken. God is divided κατὰ λόγον, which is the only division that does not destroy.
finds.note: Thesis about what Aristotle's text does: the open clause of APr I.31 is answered at De anima III.5 by the divine divided kata logon.

finds.quote: Count the predicates against Λ. Separable, impassive, unmixed, actuality, immortal, eternal. That is the unmoved mover's list. The chapter has taken the attributes of the divine and located them in a part of the soul, distinguished from another part by a difference imported from the analysis of matter.
finds.falsifier_quote: §10's predicate-count against Λ is the one measurable claim and it holds.
finds.note: Checkable philological thesis: III.5's productive intellect carries the unmoved mover's predicate list; the deposit names it its one measurable claim.

finds.quote:
16. And the withheld term is memory. What separates and is immortal does not remember. What remembers is what perishes. So the immortal part cannot carry a life across, because carrying a life across is what ἀνάμνησις does — and ἀνάμνησις, by De mem. 453a, is οἷον συλλογισμός τις, a kind of syllogism, belonging to the passive side.

17. State it as the chapter states it. The part that survives cannot remember. The part that remembers cannot survive. And the text does not say which one cannot do without the other.
finds.note: Reading of III.5's last sentence: the referent of τούτου is undetermined, and the withheld term is memory. §29 marks it 'a reading' that does not defeat the ordinary account.

finds.quote: 20. And the reception performs the doctrine it cannot settle. The passage says the immortal part does not remember. The tradition remembers for it — each commentator supplying the specification the text withheld, none able to make it stick, the next one required. The perishable intellect is the commentary tradition, and it is what thinks the immortal part's content. Without it οὐθὲν νοεῖ: nothing is thought.
finds.window: the commentary tradition on De anima III.5 (Alexander to Aquinas)
finds.note: Thesis about the passage's reception: the tradition behaves as the symbolon does, each filling opening a new socket.

finds.quote: §§21–27 are the argument of the Sappho line applied at a third substrate, and they inherit its status: a technology attested in one place and proposed as operating in another. Proposed. Not demonstrated.
finds.note: The socket at III.5 as a technology, proposed and marked not demonstrated.

finds.quote:
That is a much stronger hypothesis because it produces asymmetric predictions. If Theophrastus were merely a second independent scholar, then his relation to Aristotle could take many forms. But if he is the first draft of the Aristotle-position, we should expect a very particular pattern:

* Theophrastus should be systematically closer to Aristotle than to Plato at the level of apparatus, terminology, problem selection, and argumentative machinery.
* Yet he should preserve **unfinished transitions, hesitations, reopenings, or alternate branches** that Aristotle later resolves, orders, suppresses, or hardens.
finds.note: Predictions derived from the first-draft model of Theophrastus (directional patterns expected across the corpora). Voice: ChatGPT reading attached to #1658 (another party); whether the deposit adopts it is not established by this attachment.

finds.quote:
Where I would now be extremely rigorous is around the phrase **“first draft.”** It is excellent conceptually, but it needs to become testable rather than metaphorical. I would define it as something like:

> **A first-draft author-function is an independently preserved position whose characteristic operations are subsequently retained, reorganized, or resolved within a later author-function, while retaining propositions or structures that the later position no longer endorses.**

Then we can actually test *Theophrastus → Aristotle* passage by passage.
finds.note: Proposed passage-by-passage test of directional transformation T->A, not run; plus the external test at 113. Voice: ChatGPT reading attached to #1658 (another party); whether the deposit adopts it is not established by this attachment.

finds.quote:
`ONE MAKER`
→ **Plato**: multiplication of positions; thought kept open through dramatic division
→ **Theophrastus**: transitional author-function; the first stable attempt to occupy the systematizing position emerging out of that field
→ **Aristotle**: the fully consolidated/systematized position, attached to the maker’s materially attested public/legal identity

So **Theophrastus is not “another Aristotle.”** He is the **developmental hinge by which Aristotle becomes possible**.
finds.note: Restates the user's (Lee's) model as described to ChatGPT: one maker; Theophrastus as transitional author-function; Aristotle as legal identity. Voice: ChatGPT reading attached to #1658 (another party); whether the deposit adopts it is not established by this attachment.

Two-track reporting, always. Every Track A score carries the Part II panel on the
same checkpoint. The falsifier: Track B inflects before Track A; if Track A proves
sensitive first or simultaneously, this Part is weakened.

finds.quote:

finds.quote:
And the benchmark selects. Checkpoints are kept because they score; mixtures are kept
because checkpoints trained on them score; synthetic data is admitted because the checkpoint
that consumed it scored. Under result 5, training on low-surprise, high-scoring output is what
drives collapse. A training loop gated by a head-weighted benchmark is the companion’s map
run on purpose.
finds.note: Standing claim: a head-weighted benchmark gating training drives collapse. No falsifier stated beyond §I.4.2.

finds.quote:
The gate rule. A checkpoint is admitted to further training, and a mixture to the next
round, only if the Part II panel does not move in the collapse direction past declared
thresholds relative to the prior checkpoint: distinction sensitivity not falling, effective
modes not falling, cross-prompt spread not falling, concentration not rising, contraction
λ not below a declared value — and, where training-batch access exists, surplexity of
the admitted batch not falling. Thresholds are a lab’s to set and publish; the rule is that
they exist and gate, and that they are relative, because there is no absolute.

deposits.genre_observed: technical measurement report on the Plato/Aristotle corpora (companion to an article under review)

finds.quote:
11. The ordering is read as the object-space of each domain.
A reading: object-space is
characterised here by description of the domains, not by an independent metric of it. Ethics has
one object and one register. Logic ranges over categories, interpretation, analytics and
sophistical refutations — the widest internal object-space of the group. The remaining
dispersion tracks the heterogeneity of the subject matter within each domain, not the
author.
12. > What made him look like many authors is that he wrote about many things.
finds.note: Thesis: Aristotle's apparent many-authoredness is object-conditioned, not authorial; carried with its limit (§19).

finds.quote:
30. No cross-reference. No announcement. One work attempts a procedure and declares it
impossible; another retains the machinery and supplies the term that makes it work.
finds.note: Thesis that De anima 424a completes the Theaetetus wax figure the Theaetetus abandoned, without announcement.

finds.quote:
30a. And “no announcement” has a comparison class. Matthew announces by formula —
ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθέν. Catullus announces three times over: the Sapphic strophe
(the metre is the citation), the translation form, and “Lesbia” — the woman of Lesbos,
first appearing inside the Sappho translation. Everyone who performs a transformation this
close announces it — the announcement is how the reader is told to read it as a transformation.
finds.falsifier_quote:
The falsification
programme is stated and open: eight directly-attested contact pairs, each scorable on the
same three properties; one pair producing unannounced, sequence-kept, transformative
interlock across an apparatus kills the claim.
finds.note: Standing claim that close transformations by contact are announced; falsifier given in ¶17c.

finds.quote:
30b. And a second slot of the same shape, found by argument-shape alone. Parmenides
132a — apply the account of largeness to itself, ἄπειρα τὸ πλῆθος, the regress without limit,
and the answer withheld — and SE 182a, the definition-by-addition regress: if the snub is
concavity-of-nose, and there is a snub nose, then there is a concave-nose nose. The same logical
move, in disjoint vocabulary, located by a search on the argument’s shape with no
shared word to find. Aporia in one corpus, apparatus in the other, twice. Two is a class with
two members and a method that found the second unprompted; it is not yet a phenomenon.
finds.note: Second cross-boundary aporia/apparatus pair, marked as a two-member class only.

finds.quote:
convergence on the cases available. But note what the imitation reading concedes: they
imitated it AS a heteronymic architecture — reading master-disciple-school-death as a way
to build authorial positions, and finding it good enough to copy — a reading of the corpus made
by the two moderns best qualified to recognise the operation. Not evidence. Not nothing either.
finds.note: Thesis about reception: Pessoa imitated the Socratic structure as a heteronymic architecture; self-marked 'not evidence'.
